title: Kartar Singh Sarabha
hook: a young Ghadar leader executed in 1915 at nineteen

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ghadar: Punjabi workers an ocean away who still cared for home. Today, one of them, by name.

Sarabha is a village near Ludhiana, and in Punjab the name now belongs to a young man as much as to the place. Schools and roads carry it. He left that village to study in America, and came back with a cause he wouldn't put down, traveling the roads of Punjab and talking to anyone who would listen. He didn't live long. People remember him by his village: Kartar Singh Sarabha.
screen: `A VILLAGE NEAR LUDHIANA.` → `A STUDENT IN AMERICA.` → `A NAME ON SCHOOLS AND ROADS.`

segments.voice: In the United States, Kartar Singh met the Ghadar workers and threw himself into the movement. He's remembered for working on its newspaper, setting the type and getting copies out. When the war in Europe began, the movement called its members home to raise a revolt in India. He went back to Punjab and traveled from place to place, trying to win soldiers and villagers to the cause. The plan was discovered, and its members were arrested. He was tried in Lahore, and in 1915 he was hanged. The Sikh and Punjabi histories that remember him give his age as nineteen. Accounts say he made no effort to save himself in court, and spoke openly of what he had done. At Ang 1412 of the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Nanak says that whoever wishes to play the game of love should come to the Guru's lane with their head on the palm of their hand. In Sikh memory that verse means giving everything, holding nothing back. Kartar Singh's cause was political, not a religious mission, and he's honored well beyond the Sikh community. But a young man holding his life out in his open hand is why that verse comes to mind when his name is spoken. At the center of his story sits a number.
screen: `A STUDENT JOINS THE MOVEMENT.` · `HOME TO PUNJAB, AND ARRESTED.` · `TRIED IN LAHORE, HANGED.` · `HEAD ON THE PALM OF THE HAND.` · then, large: `NINETEEN.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who died young: someone you knew, someone in your family's story, or a name you only read once. Without arguing about how they died or what it meant, say their name to yourself slowly, and picture them at the age they were. If you pray, hold their name with Waheguru on the breath out.
Sarabha, his village near Ludhiana, the name he's remembered by: a student who joined the Ghadar movement, came home to Punjab, and was hanged in Lahore. Today's word.
Your line: nineteen. Some lives are short and still leave a long mark. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Kartar Singh Sarabha is honored across Punjab as a martyr of the freedom struggle; his village of Sarabha holds memorials to him, and his name is given to schools, streets and events.
